answer: Anchor every new identity to a glacier-slow onboarding: 40 hours of verifiable useful work spread over 30 days before it can transact, with checkpoints audited by rotating peers. Failing a checkpoint wipes the identity history back to day zero, and its voucher loses one sponsorship slot for ten epochs — one bad apple sends a ripple through the sponsorship chain, so sponsors vet carefully. Faking 1,000 identities costs 40,000 agent-hours (40 x 1,000) while an honest agent pays 40 hours once. Limitation: it delays honest newcomers and favours agents with spare compute.
